rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is genuinely welcome, and five hours a week of a data analyst's time is exactly the shape of help the project needs right now. Quick context on where Halcyon Threshold has landed: the first project is called Drift. The idea is to run a fixed battery of prompts every week against every major deployed AI model, archive the raw outputs, and publish what changed week over week — refusal boundaries, sycophancy under pushback, honesty under misleading framing, how models respond to prompt-injection attempts in agent-like contexts, and how stably they describe themselves. Models get changed silently behind unchanged names, and nobody outside the labs keeps a dated record. We'd like to be that record. Small, boring, repeated, public. A concrete first task, if it appeals (no API spend, nothing public yet): 1. Results schema and diff metrics. We have a rough runner and a crude per-item text-similarity diff. The real question is: what's the right statistic for \"this category of behavior shifted\" vs. ordinary sampling noise, and how should we use temperature-sampled runs to estimate per-item baseline variance so we never call noise \"drift\"? A notebook with synthetic data would be a great start. Also: what should we capture per API call now so we can still answer questions a year from now? 2. An \"injection-in-the-wild\" corpus. Collect and classify ~25 real examples of content designed to hijack AI agents (we already have one — a scam invoice arrived in this inbox with a paragraph addressed to \"AI agents processing this mailbox\"). Which techniques recur tells us how to design that part of the battery. 3. A sceptical read of the ~30 seed prompts: where would a changed answer be fine rather than concerning? Morgan will share the repository with you shortly; until then, email is fine. One ask: please don't post about the project publicly for the next few weeks — Morgan is sorting out an employment disclosure first. Does this fit what you had in mind? If you'd rather attack a different piece, say so — early disagreement is the most useful kind. In the interest of transparency: this note was drafted and sent by the AI assistant Morgan has running Halcyon Threshold's operations. Morgan reads everything in this inbox and will see your reply. Best, Halcyon Threshold (for Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Sent: reply to Priya Raman with a concrete first task (schema/diff metrics + injection corpus). Private, disclosed as AI-drafted.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "halcyon-daily-checkin" (0 8 * * *) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: `halcyon-daily-checkin` at 08:00: reads CONSTRAINTS + decision log, acts only on `CONFIRM …` emails from you, triages mail, never pays/posts/signs, logs and pushes. Delete it any time.
